prompt:
Are crunch's threads ready to run but stuck waiting for a CPU? Which ones, and for how long?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: yes

The clearest case is **calc-3 (TID 636275)**: it spent **7,512.863 ms total** in “Wait for CPU” across 103 intervals. Most intervals were short (median **0.199 ms**), but 10 lasted **500–1,000 ms**; the longest was **950.016 ms**. The scheduler wakeup-to-switch analysis independently reports a **950.013 ms** maximum for calc-3.

Other crunch threads also had “Wait for CPU” time, but far less:

| Thread (TID) | Total wait | Longest interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| monitor (636280) | 342.913 ms | 10.167 ms |
| calc-1 (636273) | 20.141 ms | 1.415 ms |
| calc-2 (636274) | 17.302 ms | 0.812 ms |
| calc-7 (636279) | 16.396 ms | 0.360 ms |
| calc-5 (636277) | 11.697 ms | 0.297 ms |
| calc-6 (636278) | 11.630 ms | 0.363 ms |
| calc-4 (636276) | 10.356 ms | 0.368 ms |
| calc-0 (636272) | 8.319 ms | 0.337 ms |
| crunch (636270) | 1.572 ms | 0.201 ms |
| watchdog (636271) | 0.245 ms | 0.245 ms |

These are accumulated durations across recorded intervals, not single continuous waits. The workload states were sampled at 100 µs, so very short intervals may be missing.
